title: Session-aware ephemeral canary reservoir with preemptive shelving
text:
Session-aware ephemeral canary reservoir with preemptive shelving

description:
Adds a lightweight 'ephemeral reservoir' to the rollout controller that reserves throttled capacity for session-aware canaries and preemptively 'shelves' (pauses) canary lanes when latency or error signals indicate imminent SLO degradation. Motivation: we observed oscillation and noisy failures when multiple small canaries competed for burst capacity under tail-latency spikes. This PR introduces a reservation token pool, a short-lived shelving lease, and a latency-hedging admission heuristic to keep canary impact bounded. Implementation notes: - New RolloutController subcomponent (reservoir manager) that tracks reservation tokens by cohort/session affinity and can grant temporary exclusive tokens to canaries. - Shelving logic: when rolling average P99 latency or error-rate derivative exceeds configured thresholds, the controller will preemptively shelve active ephemeral canaries for a configurable hold window instead of immediately escalating traffic. - Admission & hedging: requests routed to a canary lane while the reservoir is depleted are auto-hedged to baseline variant with a probabilistic sampling rate that decays as tokens free up. - API: rollout spec gains optional fields: reservoir.window_ms, reservoir.token_count, reservoir.shelve_thresholds (latency_pct, error_derivative), reservoir.hedge_sample. These are backward-compatible defaults. - Observability: new metrics (rollout_reservoir_tokens_available, rollout_shelve_events_total, rollout_hedge_routed_total) and a dashboard added in docs. - Safety: shelving is non-destructive and annotated in audit logs; canaries can be resumed manually or automatically after the hold window. Single-line checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit tests, [x] integration smoke, [x] docs update, [x] e2e canary repro harness. Related Linear: ENG-3245, ENG-8249. Related incident: SUP-87 (latency spike, hotfix Q1).

review_comments:
Priya Nair: Can we avoid a hot-path allocation for every request when hedging? Suggest using a sampled fastpath and share a per-worker RNG. — Author reply: switched to per-worker RNG and added microbench showing <1us overhead.
Mateo Ruiz: The default token_count=3 seems low for some high-throughput customers; recommend making this cluster-scoped default conservative and document how to tune. — Author reply: increased default to 8 and added tuning guide to docs/reservoir.md.
Claire Zhang: Need clearer audit annotations so SRE can attribute auto-shelving events to rollout decisions. — Author reply: added shelving annotations to rollout audit log and surfaced a telemetry tag in metrics.
Omar Haddad (optional): Integration test flaked on CI due to timing; please stabilize. — Author reply: adjusted the test harness sleep and added deterministic token expiry override in test mode.

release_notes:
Introduces 'ephemeral reservoir' for session-aware canaries: safety-first reservation tokens, preemptive shelving policy, and latency-hedged routing. Administrators can tune reservoir.* fields on rollout specs. See docs/rollouts/reservoir.md for defaults and tuning guidance.
